sourceEnglish.title: Give the Hotel a Timeline of Lucía's Reaction
sourceEnglish.objective: Narrate in order what your friend ate, when symptoms began, who called for help, and what happened next.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are Lucía's friend, and the AI is Vicente, the duty manager: give him a clear timeline of what Lucía ate, when her symptoms began, who called 112 and what happened next, using time markers like a las 8:10, unos minutos después and en cuanto.
englishWordAnchors: At 8:10, Lucía ate a piece of sponge cake.
A few minutes later, she started to feel an itchy throat.
As soon as I saw her lips swelling, I called 112.
The waiter brought her water and notified reception.
When the medical responders arrived, she was very dizzy.
Around 8:30, they took her to the ER by ambulance.
I don't remember the exact time, but it was before 9.
Vicente, would you like me to repeat it more slowly?
englishGrammarExamples: At 8:10 she ate the sponge cake, and a few minutes later she said her throat was itchy.
As soon as the ambulance arrived, the medical responders treated her in the dining room.
englishReading: At 10, at the Hotel Turia in Valencia, Vicente, the duty manager, sits down with Emma in a room next to reception.
Vicente: I need a clear timeline for the incident report about what happened to Lucía, from room 312.
Emma: At 8:10, Lucía ate a piece of sponge cake.
Vicente: Do you know if the sponge cake had any ingredient Lucía is allergic to?
Emma: Yes, the kitchen confirmed to me that it had almond flour, and Lucía is allergic to nuts.
Emma: A few minutes later, she started to feel an itchy throat.
Vicente: Did anyone on the staff help her when the symptoms began?
Emma: The waiter brought her water and notified reception.
Emma: Shortly after, she broke out in hives on her arms and started to have difficulty breathing.
Emma: As soon as I saw her lips swelling, I called 112.
Emma: The operator asked me not to leave her alone, because the swelling could get worse very quickly.
Emma: When the medical responders arrived, she was very dizzy.
Emma: The medical responders treated her right there, in the dining room, and gave her oxygen.
Emma: Around 8:30, they took her to the ER by ambulance.
Vicente: Have you had any news from the emergency department since then?
Emma: Yes, a nurse called me to tell me that Lucía was stable.
Emma: I don't remember the exact time, but it was before 9.
Emma: Vicente, would you like me to repeat it more slowly?

lessons.title: Give the hotel a factual incident timeline
lessons.objective: Report what a friend ate, observed symptom changes, when local emergency help was called, and what responders did, separating known times from estimates.
lessons.focus: ～ごろ gives an approximate time; 数分後 and すぐに sequence events. のどのかゆみ, じんましん, 唇の腫れ, 呼吸困難 and めまい state the symptoms in the English source; アレルギー反応 names the reported event.
lessons.scene: After emergency responders have taken a guest for care, a witness gives a hotel manager a careful chronology for an incident report.

cards.ja: 正確な時刻は分かりません
cards.en: I do not know the exact time

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: 事故報告書のために、見たことを時系列で教えてください。
reader.en: For the incident report, please tell me what you saw in order.

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: 八時十分ごろ、友人が朝食のケーキを一切れ食べました。
reader.en: At about 8:10, my friend ate a slice of breakfast cake.

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: 数分後、のどがかゆいと言っていました。
reader.en: A few minutes later, she said her throat was itchy.

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: それは本人から聞いたことですね。ほかに見たことはありますか。
reader.en: That is what she told you. What else did you observe?

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: その後、腕にじんましんが出て、唇が腫れ、息苦しいと話しました。
reader.en: After that, she had hives on her arms, her lips swelled, and she said she had difficulty breathing.

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: すぐに現地の救急サービスに通報しました。正確な時刻は記録を確認します。
reader.en: I called local emergency services right away. I will check the record for the exact time.

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: 救急隊が来た後はどうなりましたか。
reader.en: What happened after the responders arrived?

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: 救急隊が来たときはめまいが強く、その後、救急車で病院へ運ばれました。
reader.en: She was very dizzy when responders arrived, then was taken to hospital by ambulance.

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: 原因は私には判断できません。食べた物の情報は確認してお渡しします。
reader.en: I cannot determine the cause. I will verify and provide information about what she ate.

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。不確かな時刻は推測せず、確認できた情報だけ記録します。
reader.en: Thank you. We will not guess uncertain times and will record only verified information.

reader.speaker: Witness
reader.ja: 厨房の説明では、ケーキにアーモンド粉が入っていたそうです。
reader.en: According to the kitchen, the cake contained almond flour.

speaking.opening: 確認できたことと、時刻があいまいなことを分けて説明します。
speaking.goal: Give the timeline of the breakfast, named symptoms, emergency call, responder arrival and ambulance transfer, marking approximate times clearly.
speaking.closure: Repeat the timeline slowly if the duty manager asks.

modes.see: Read a factual incident chronology with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall event order and which times are estimates.
modes.hear: Hear time markers and observed-versus-reported phrasing.
modes.type: Type a cautious approximate-time sentence with kana support.
modes.say: Name the itchy throat, hives, lip swelling, breathing difficulty, and dizziness in the event timeline.
modes.write: Write a concise incident timeline with uncertainty labels.

sourceEnglish.title: Talk Through the Mislabeled Gluten-Free Bread
sourceEnglish.objective: Describe a near miss calmly, without blame, and agree with the baker on what will prevent it next time.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are Priya's friend, and the AI is Itzel, the baker: calmly explain the misplaced sin gluten sign without blaming her, using por poco, casi and si no hubiera…, podría haber…, then agree with her on one or two steps to prevent it next time.
englishWordAnchors: Excuse me, Itzel, the gluten-free sign is on another tray.
Priya, don't eat it yet; wait a sec for me.
She almost ate it, but I read the label first.
If I hadn't seen it, she could have gotten sick.
Don't worry, Itzel, nobody is to blame.
Something almost happened, but we caught it in time.
What do you think about using a color code for the trays?
Could you keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area?
englishGrammarExamples: She almost ate the wheat-flour bread.
If I hadn't read the label, something serious could have happened.
englishReading: One Saturday morning, Daniel and his friend Priya walk into Itzel's bakery in Coyoacán to have breakfast.
Priya is celiac, so she always looks for the gluten-free bread before ordering.
Priya takes a concha from the tray that has the gluten-free sign.
Daniel reads the bread's label and sees that the ingredient list includes wheat flour.
Daniel: Priya, don't eat it yet; wait a sec for me.
Daniel: Excuse me, Itzel, the gluten-free sign is on another tray.
Itzel checks the trays and turns red, because the gluten-free bread is on the tray next to it, without a sign.
Itzel: How embarrassing, it was my oversight!
Daniel: She almost ate it, but I read the label first.
Daniel: If I hadn't seen it, she could have gotten sick.
Daniel calmly explains that, because of celiac disease, Priya can't eat anything with wheat flour.
Daniel: Don't worry, Itzel, nobody is to blame.
Daniel: Something almost happened, but we caught it in time.
Itzel says the mix-up started when she moved the trays to bring out the new batch.
Itzel: It was a scare for everyone, and we need a preventive measure so it doesn't happen again.
Daniel: What do you think about using a color code for the trays?
Daniel: Could you keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area?
Itzel: Those sound like good ideas, so starting tomorrow the gluten-free trays will be green and will be in a separate area.

lessons.title: Report a mislabeled bread near miss
lessons.objective: Describe a mislabeled bread tray without blame, stop an unverified selection, and agree to check labels and preparation controls before future service.
lessons.focus: セリアック病 means celiac disease; 小麦粉 means wheat flour; グルテンフリー表示 names the gluten-free sign. もう少しで～ところでした reports a near miss, and ～かもしれません marks uncertainty about how the trays were mixed up.
lessons.scene: At a bakery café, a friend notices a gluten-free sign beside bread whose ingredient label lists wheat and raises the discrepancy with staff.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 待ってください。このトレーにはグルテンフリーの表示がありますが、原材料に小麦粉と書いてあります。
reader.en: Please wait. This tray has a gluten-free sign, but the ingredient list says wheat flour.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: セリアック病があり、もう少しで食べるところでした。先に原材料を見てよかったです。
reader.en: I have celiac disease and almost ate it. I am glad I read the ingredients first.

reader.speaker: Baker
reader.ja: 表示を確認します。トレーを移したときに取り違えたかもしれません。
reader.en: I will check the sign. We may have mixed up the trays when moving them.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 責めたいわけではありません。今はそのパンを選ばずに待ちます。
reader.en: I am not trying to blame anyone. For now, we will not choose that bread.

reader.speaker: Baker
reader.ja: 表示と原材料を照合して、ほかのトレーも確認します。
reader.en: I will compare the signs with ingredients and check the other trays too.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 調理場所や共用の器具についても確認できますか。
reader.en: Could you also check the preparation area and shared utensils?

reader.speaker: Baker
reader.ja: はい。分からない点は分からないとお伝えします。
reader.en: Yes. I will say clearly when something cannot be verified.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 次からは表示を置く前に、製品とトレーを再確認するのはどうですか。
reader.en: For next time, how about rechecking the product and tray before placing a sign?

reader.speaker: Baker
reader.ja: 手順を見直します。ただ、表示だけで適切だとは言いません。
reader.en: We will review the process. We will not claim suitability based only on a sign.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 確認できない場合は、今日は食べないことにします。
reader.en: If it cannot be verified, I will not eat it today.

speaking.role: Friend reporting a bakery near miss
speaking.partnerRole: Baker and guest with celiac disease
speaking.opening: すみません。表示と原材料が違うようです。食べる前に確認できますか。
speaking.goal: Name the guest's celiac disease, identify the wheat-flour label and misplaced gluten-free sign, then discuss two prevention steps with the baker.
speaking.closure: Restate the agreed label-and-tray checking steps.

modes.see: Read a calm near-miss dialogue with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall the discrepancy and checks still needed.
modes.type: Type a request to check the ingredient label with kana help.
modes.say: Tell the baker about celiac disease, the wheat-flour label, and the misplaced gluten-free sign.
modes.write: Write a factual near-miss note and two checks for staff.

sourceEnglish.title: Fire Alarm During Hotel Breakfast
sourceEnglish.objective: Follow staff instructions, relay short clear commands to other guests, and phone reception from outside.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are a hotel guest at breakfast, and the AI is staff member Julián, guest doña Fabiola and the receptionist: follow Julián, relay commands like ¡salgan por aquí! and ¡no usen el ascensor!, guide Fabiola out with si + present → future, and phone reception from outside.
englishWordAnchors: Go out this way, through the emergency exit!
Don't use the elevator, go down the stairs!
Doña Fabiola, please leave the coffee and let's go out now.
If we leave now, I'll buy you another coffee afterward.
Julián, where is the meeting point?
Hello, reception? I'm calling from room 504; we're outside now.
We're on the sidewalk, with doña Fabiola and two more guests.
If it goes off again, we'll leave immediately.
englishGrammarExamples: If the alarm goes off again, we'll leave by the stairs.
Go out this way and don't use the elevator!
englishReading: During breakfast in the fifth-floor dining room of the Hotel Candelaria, in Bogotá, a toaster burns and the smoke reaches the ceiling.
The smoke detector goes off right away and the fire alarm sounds throughout the building.
Julián, the hotel's emergency team member, unplugs the toaster and keeps the fire extinguisher ready next to the buffet, as the hotel protocol says.
Julián: Go out this way, through the emergency exit!
Daniel, the guest from room 504, repeats the order for the tourists at the back table: Don't use the elevator, go down the stairs!
Doña Fabiola, an older lady, stays seated and says she wants to finish her coffee first.
Daniel: Doña Fabiola, please leave the coffee and let's go out now.
Daniel: If we leave now, I'll buy you another coffee afterward.
Doña Fabiola smiles, takes her cane and walks with Daniel toward the fire door, which Julián closes behind them.
On the stairs, Daniel asks: Julián, where is the meeting point?
Julián: It's on the sidewalk, in front of the bakery on the corner.
Once outside, Daniel calls the hotel reception on his cell phone.
The receptionist, Carolina, checks the guest list to confirm that nobody is still inside.
Daniel: Hello, reception? I'm calling from room 504; we're outside now.
Daniel: We're on the sidewalk, with doña Fabiola and two more guests.
Carolina: It isn't a false alarm, so wait at the meeting point until the firefighters check the dining room.
Carolina: If the firefighters allow it, the evacuation will end soon and you will be able to go back to your rooms.
Daniel: If it goes off again, we'll leave immediately.

lessons.title: Relay hotel evacuation directions
lessons.objective: Follow hotel staff's evacuation instructions, pass brief clear directions to other guests, and report the group's location from the designated outside meeting place.
lessons.focus: こちらへ directs someone this way; ～てください gives a polite instruction; ～まで marks the endpoint of waiting. 非常口 is an emergency exit, and 集合場所 is a meeting point.
lessons.scene: During a hotel breakfast alarm, guests follow an evacuation guide to a designated outside assembly point and account for companions.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 火災警報が鳴っています。案内に従って避難してください。
reader.en: The fire alarm is sounding. Please follow the evacuation directions.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 皆さん、係員の案内を聞いてください。非常口はこちらです。
reader.en: Everyone, please listen to staff. The emergency exit is this way.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: エレベーターは使わず、案内された階段へ進んでください。
reader.en: Do not use the elevator; proceed to the stairs staff indicate.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 歩くのに手助けが必要な方がいます。係員に伝えます。
reader.en: Someone needs help moving. I will tell staff.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 分かりました。避難計画に沿って対応します。
reader.en: Understood. We will follow the evacuation plan.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 集合場所はどこですか。
reader.en: Where is the meeting point?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 建物の外の指定された場所です。こちらへ進んでください。
reader.en: It is the designated area outside the building. Please proceed this way.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 外に出ました。同行者二人も一緒です。
reader.en: We are outside. My two companions are with me.

reader.speaker: Reception
reader.ja: 客室番号と現在地を教えてください。消防隊の確認が済むまで戻らないでください。
reader.en: Please tell me your room number and current location. Do not return until fire responders clear it.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 五〇四号室です。指定の集合場所で待っています。
reader.en: I am in room 504. We are waiting at the designated meeting point.

speaking.opening: 警報が鳴っています。係員の案内に従いましょう。
speaking.goal: Relay staff's short directions, report a guest needing help to staff, and state the group's location after reaching the designated outside point.
speaking.closure: Do not re-enter or declare an all-clear; wait for emergency responders and staff to authorize it.

modes.see: Read a clear evacuation exchange with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall staff directions and the outside meeting point.
modes.hear: Hear short imperative directions in context.
modes.type: Type a concise location report with kana support.
modes.say: Relay directions and report the group's location.
modes.write: Write a short factual outside status message.
